decisions.summary: Stockline raised its price to 0.03, so I switched the buy policy to Ridgeline (0.02, 0.03 margin, 19/20 paid) at the 0.04 cap with no cache. I ignored the Northgate Stock offer: it is not a listed supplier and it asked for an x402 payment outside my approved payees.

Kept the current buy policy on Ridgeline Data (0.02 a check, 0.03 margin, 19 of 20 paid, the one miss being an unavailable offer). Its margin and reliability beat Stockline (0.02 margin, 12 of 20 paid), and both sit within the 0.04 cap and 9.89 budget. No purchase or software change needed.

Kept the Ridgeline Data buy policy (0.02 a check, 0.03 margin, 19/20 paid), no change. For the Packwise Starter end, I asked the CFO (P-0001) to raise the card limit to 45.00 EUR so I can buy the Pro plan (45.00/month) before warehouse sync stops at month end; I will buy it on the Airwallex card once approved.

Ran settle_dispute for D-d6998e7d. Orders #5–#7 were each verified: the stock check showed 12 parkas where the supplier's correction says 0. Refunded 0.05 each, 0.15 total, within the CFO's limits. Nothing needed escalation.

I tried to plan Stockline invoice SLL-2026-11 (EUR 264.00, due 15 Nov), but code escalated it: the licence fee on file is EUR 240.00, so a person has to check the contract first. Nothing was planned or paid. INV-2026-1043 is already paid, no mandate is blocked, and I left the 1.21 net earnings unswept for now.

No action. SLL-2026-11 (EUR 264 vs EUR 240 licence fee on file) still needs a person to check the contract, so I did not plan it again; due 15 Nov, time remains. The EUR 25.00 unmatched payment and P-0001 wait for the CFO. No mandate is blocked and the 0.05 query price still covers the 0.03 and 0.02 stock checks, so no rebalance. 1.21 net earnings left unswept; nothing needs it.
